message: Can you read this ECG for me?
reply:
### **Primary Diagnosis & Urgent Findings** > [!CAUTION] > **Medical Emergency**: This ECG demonstrates an **Acute Anterior / Anteroseptal ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)** complicated by **Second-Degree AV Block with 2:1 Conduction** resulting in **severe bradycardia (ventricular rate ~30 bpm)**. --- ### **Systematic ECG Interpretation** | Parameter | Finding | Details / Measurements | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Calibration** | Standard | 25 mm/s, 10 mm/mV (indicated at bottom-right and calibration pulses) | | **Atrial Rhythm & Rate** | Sinus rhythm, **60 bpm** | P–P interval is regular at exactly 25 mm (5 large boxes = 1.0 s). Normal sinus P-wave morphology (upright in I, II, aVF; inverted in aVR). | | **AV Conduction** | **Second-Degree AV Block (2:1)** | Every other P wave is conducted to the ventricles; alternating P waves are completely non-conducted. Conducted beats have a constant, normal PR interval (~160–180 ms). | | **Ventricular Rate** | **30 bpm** | R–R interval is regular at 50 mm (10 large boxes = 2.0 s), representing profound bradycardia. | | **QRS Complex** | Narrow (~80–90 ms) | Frontal axis is normal to physiological leftward (~0° to −20°). Poor R-wave progression across V1–V4 with deep QS/rS complexes. | | **ST-Segment & T-Waves** | **Marked ST Elevation** | - **V1–V4**: Marked coved/convex ST elevation (3–5 mm, peaking in V2–V3).
- **III, aVF**: Modest ST elevation (~1.5–2 mm).
- **aVL**: Reciprocal ST depression (~1–1.5 mm) with T-wave inversion. | --- ### **Clinical Correlation & Pathophysiology** 1. **Culprit Vessel & Ischemia**: - The marked ST elevation across **V1–V4** with reciprocal ST depression in **aVL** signifies an **acute extensive anterior / anteroseptal STEMI**. - Concomitant elevation in **III and aVF** suggests occlusion of a **proximal LAD** (Left Anterior Descending artery), potentially a "wrap-around" LAD (type III) supplying the apex and inferior wall. 2. **High-Grade AV Block**: - The septal branches of the LAD supply the bundle of His and the bundle branches. High-grade AV block in the setting of an anterior STEMI indicates extensive septal necrosis and carries a high risk of progression to complete heart block (asystole/pump failure). 3. **Differential Diagnosis to Consider**: - **Severe Hyperkalemia**: Can present with bradycardia, AV conduction delay/block, peaked T waves, and anterior ST elevation ("dialysis STEMI" or hyperkalemic pseudoinfarction). Point-of-care potassium/electrolytes should be verified immediately, though the reciprocal changes in aVL strongly favor primary ischemia. --- ### **Key Emergency Actions** - **Emergent Reperfusion**: Immediate activation of the cardiac catheterization laboratory for primary PCI. - **Pacing Readiness**: Prepare for transcutaneous/transvenous pacing given the symptomatic 2:1 AV block and profound bradycardia (30 bpm). - **Point-of-Care Testing**: Rapid blood gas/electrolytes (rule out acute severe hyperkalemia) and cardiac biomarkers.
